question: Can analytical per-pixel maximum-safe scaling retain the CB8 characteristic residual while preventing new hard-boundary crossings and preserving photographic ordering without hard clipping?

operator.compiled_curve: exact CB8 three-channel mean normalized-transmittance PCHIP; no refit
operator.raw_residual: r = nominal_strength * (curve(x) - x) independently in linear RGB
operator.safe_execution: one shared per-pixel alpha in [0,1], analytically maximized so every source-interior channel remains strictly inside the frozen epsilon boundaries along r
operator.hue_contract: the same alpha scales all three residual components; no per-channel clipping or post-hoc gamut compression
operator.boundary_contract: source values already within an epsilon boundary are not moved farther outward; source-interior values cannot newly enter either epsilon boundary

controls.cb8_raw: unchanged channelwise 20 percent characteristic candidate before analytical scaling
controls.joint_basic: per-image joint EV/WB/contrast/saturation fit on the exact sample from source to candidate
controls.source_boundary: new epsilon boundary relative to source
controls.gradient: linear-RGB p99.9 gradient magnitude and adjacent material L-star sign inversion

stop_rules: Do not change curve, nominal strength, safe-scale formula, boundary epsilon, source population, basic control or gates after candidate pixels are scored.
Any automatic or confirmed severe-artifact failure closes this exact analytical executor without strength, epsilon, curve, source or threshold rescue.

Pass may retain only a generic bounded film-inspired colour-tone mechanism for a fresh direct comparison with fixed AO6; it cannot establish Velvia calibration, scene exposure, dye colour, authenticity, preference or product promotion.
claim_ceiling: Rights-cleared photographic development evidence for analytical gamut-safe residual execution of a retained first-party reversal characteristic shape; not Velvia calibration, stock colour, scene exposure, authenticity, preference or product promotion.
